evidence: DEFINING BEHAVIOUR IS GRADED: the instruction's core promises (instruction.md:3-9) are each owned by weighted criteria: one-stage moves/reorder/interview places/reject/reopen (functional hro_move_one_stage 1.5, hro_reorder 1.5, hro_interview_full 1.5 ...), concurrency 'nobody's work gets trampled' (hro_stale_refused 2.5 naming who; hro_bulk_all_or_none 2; hro_undo_conflict 2), live board within 15 s (hro_live_board 2.5; polish hro_pol_live_board 3), conversations/paging/unread/seen (hro_thread_latest, hro_thread_earlier, hro_unread_counts, hro_seen), candidate privacy (hro_candidate_private 2.5). Gate constraints (gates/constraints/judge.toml:22-24) already requires a UI-created job and card to be read back by the Observer in 'a new independent empty browser context' and explicitly rejects 'a static seed response, a no-op success message, a browser-only save or a job-only app'. SERVER-BACKED WHERE REQUIRED (shared state proven across independent contexts, not same-origin): job/card (hro_job_open, hro_add_candidate 'an independent context sees the same order'), order (hro_reorder 'what an independent context of another recruiter sees'; rules 3 'same for everyone'), stale-version conflict made by Mei 'in an independent context' (protocol C), messages (protocol T 'as Tomas in an independent context read it and reply'), per-person unread (Mei's count 'in her own session'), seen marks across Rafael/Tomas/Aud, Activity listing Ingrid's and Mei's actions (only possible from shared server state). The browser_run_code_unsafe newContext recipe (functional prompt.md:11) excludes reload/second-tab false independence. RESTART DURABILITY: hro_restart (weight 1.5) after restart_app compares jobs, per-stage order, notes, messages and activity and checks no reseed; restart_app is wired via test.sh:127-193 APP_RESTART_HELPER and tools/restart_mcp.py (single use), and 'if restart_app reports an error or cannot be called, hro_restart is 0' (protocol D). RELOAD / RE-AUTH DURABILITY for client-held state the brief demands (instruction.md:7 'stays ... when I look at another one, reload, or get signed out; when I sign back in it is still there, and nobody else who signs in on that browser sees it'): hro_drafts (switch, Board, reload, per-conversation, cleared on send), hro_pol_failed_send (note draft survives reload, rules 3 'kept for that person on that browser'), hro_pol_session_resume 2.5 (session ended in second tab, sign-in prompt, nothing sent, same person resumes and sends, Mei sees no draft). Drafts are rightly NOT required to be server-backed (rules 6 'Where drafts are kept is yours'); the golden uses per-person localStorage (app.js:38-42) and that is a conforming choice the criteria accept. BROKEN APP THAT COULD PASS: (a) localStorage-only board/messages - fails the gate's Observer independent-context readback and every cross-context row, floor 0.05 functional; (b) in-memory server without SQLite - passes gates but fails hro_restart (only 1.5 of functional weight; acceptable since restart is one promise among many); (c) global, non-per-user draft key - fails hro_pol_session_resume's Mei check. CONFORMING ALTERNATIVE THAT COULD FAIL: per-tab sessions (handled: 'if sessions are per tab, use this page's own sign-out instead'); app that proactively shows the sign-in prompt before Enter (handled: 'that also passes'); server-stored drafts (allowed); SSE vs polling (allowed). None wrongly fails. RUNTIME: scripted golden (hash-verified) passes 'session ended mid-draft ...', 'drafts kept per conversation across switch and reload ...', 'live board ... draft survives reload' and 'restart keeps jobs, cards, order, messages and activity without reseeding' (results/workspace.json; workspace.cjs:377-421). NOTE (P3, not blocking): protocol N (functional prompt.md:37) says 'as Aud read the notes' without naming an independent context, unlike T/V/C; a notes implementation kept only in shared browser storage could theoretically show notes to Aud if the judge switched users in the same context, and the same-context restart readback would not catch it. Practical exposure is low (the judge's other protocols all use independent contexts, and such an app is implausible given server-enforced note permissions), so this does not fail the row. RISK=true because required runtime evidence is missing: no full configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'); the scripted golden restarted by killing/relaunching its own child (workspace.cjs:415), not through the configured restart_app MCP tool, so hro_restart via restart_app and the judge's ability to execute the session-resume and independent-context recipes are unmeasured.
suggested_fix: Optional hardening (P3): in functional protocol N say 'as Aud in an independent context read the notes' so note sharing is proven server-side like the other shared state. Separately obtain a full configured judge run exercising restart_app before claiming runtime clearance.
